title: Tailwind vs Traditional CSS
definition: A comparison between Semantic CSS (naming classes based on content) and Utility-First CSS (naming classes based on visual function).
simpleExplanation: Traditional CSS focuses on 'What is this element?' (`.author-bio`). Tailwind focuses on 'What does this element look like?' (`.font-bold .text-gray-500`). This solves the problem of having 50 different classes across your app that all just apply `display: flex`.
realWorldExample: In traditional CSS, if you change `.author-bio` to make the text blue, you might accidentally break the blog layout because someone reused `.author-bio` on the footer. In Tailwind, changes are strictly localized to the specific HTML element you are touching.

basic: Does Tailwind require you to invent class names like `outer-wrapper`?
intermediate: What is the 'Global Scope' problem in traditional CSS that Tailwind solves?

answers.question: Invent class names?
answers.answer: No! That is one of its biggest benefits. Naming things is the hardest part of computer science. Tailwind eliminates the need to invent semantic class names entirely.

answers.question: Global Scope problem?
answers.answer: In traditional CSS, all styles are global. Adding a new rule might unintentionally override something elsewhere. Tailwind classes are single-purpose and applied locally in the HTML, making unexpected side-effects impossible.
